AWARD 


Matter placed today before Tribunal for order. perused the record. This industrial dispute was received 
from Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L-12012/170/2000-IR(B.T) dated 19.9.2000 which 
has been referred under section 10(1)(d) of the 1.2. Act, 1947 for adjudication, to Industrial Tribunal No.I, Hyderabad 
for adjudication and later the same has been transferred to this Tribunal bearing ID No. 114/2000, as per orders of 
Central Government vide Lr.No.H-11026/1/2001-IR(C.ID dated 18.10.2001, requiring this forum to decide the 
question: 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of State Bank of India, Vijayawada Zone in dismissing the services 
of Sri D. Arjuna Rao, Ex-Messenger, is justified? If not, what relief the workman is entitled?” 


After receipt of the reference, it was numbered as ID No. 132/2002 and notices were issued to both the 
Workman and the management. 


2. The perusal of the claim statement filed by the Petitioner as well as the counter of the Respondent goes to 
reveal that this matter pertains to the termination of the Petitioner from service by the Respondent. The Appropriate 
government has not referred any industrial dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication in respect of termination of 
Petitioner. 


Section 10 (4) provides:- 


“10(4):-Where in an order referring an industrial dispute to [a Labour Court, Tribunal or National 
Tribunal] under this section or in a subsequent order, the appropriate Government has specified the points of 
dispute for adjudication, [the Labour Court or the Tribunal or the National Tribunal, as the case may 
be,] shall confine its adjudication to those points and matters incidental thereto.” 


Thus, in view of the above provision the Industrial Tribunal cannot decide a dispute not explicitly referred to 
it by the appropriate Government as it’s jurisdiction under Section 10 (4) of ID Act, 1947 is confined to the specific 
point of dispute mentioned in the reference order and matter incidental there to. If the reference is for dismissal but 
the matter pertains to the termination, the Tribunal must strictly stick to the referred terms. 


3. Therefore, in view of the provision contained under Section 10(4) of the I.D.Act, 1947, there is no reference 
of the industrial dispute regarding termination of the Petitioner for adjudication before this Tribunal. The reference of 
dispute herein pertain to the dismissal of the Petitioner from service. Therefore, this Tribunal cannot adjudicate the 
dispute in the absence of reference of termination by retrenchment of Petitioner. 


4. Even otherwise, Petitioner workman has failed to substantiate his claim of 240 days of continuous service 
in a calendar year just preceding from the date of his termination by any evidence in terms of mandate of Sec.25F of 
I.D.Act, 1947. Therefore, the claim of the Petitioner that he has been terminated illegally is not tenable and he is 
not entitled to any relief as claimed in the claim statement. Thus, Reference is answered accordingly. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.

Matter placed today before Tribunal for order. perused the record. This industrial dispute was received 
from Government of India, Ministry of Labour by its order No. L-12012/158/2000-IR(B.I)_ dated 31.8.2000 which 
has been referred under section 10(1)(d) of the 1.2. Act, 1947 for adjudication, to Industrial Tribunal No.I, Hyderabad 
for adjudication and later the same has been transferred to this Tribunal bearing ID No. 111/2000, as per orders of 
Central Government vide Lr.No.H-11026/1/2001-IR(C.ID dated 18.10.2001, requiring this forum to decide the 
question: 


SCHEDULE 


“Whether the action of the management of State Bank of India, Tirupathi Zone in dismissing the services of 
Sri P. Subramanyeswara Rao, Ex-Messenger, w.e.f. 31.3.1997 is justified? If not, what relief the workman 
is entitled?” 


After receipt of the reference, it was numbered as ID No. 66/2002 and notices were issued to both the 
Workman and the management. 


25 The perusal of the claim statement filed by the Petitioner as well as the counter of the Respondent goes to 
reveal that this matter pertains to the termination of the Petitioner from service by the Respondent. The Appropriate 
government has not referred any industrial dispute to this Tribunal for adjudication in respect of termination of 
Petitioner. 


Section 10 (4) provides:- 


“10(4):-Where in an order referring an industrial dispute to [a Labour Court, Tribunal or National 
Tribunal] under this section or in a subsequent order, the appropriate Government has specified the points of 
dispute for adjudication, [the Labour Court or the Tribunal or the National Tribunal, as the case may 
be,] shall confine its adjudication to those points and matters incidental thereto.” 


Thus, in view of the above provision the Industrial Tribunal cannot decide a dispute not explicitly referred to 
it by the appropriate Government as it’s jurisdiction under Section 10 (4) of ID Act, 1947 is confined to the specific 
point of dispute mentioned in the reference order and matter incidental there to. If the reference is for dismissal but 
the matter pertains to the termination, the Tribunal must strictly stick to the referred terms. 


3. Therefore, in view of the provision contained under Section 10(4) of the I.D.Act, 1947, there is no reference 
of the industrial dispute regarding termination of the Petitioner for adjudication before this Tribunal. The reference of 
dispute herein pertain to the dismissal of the Petitioner from service. Therefore, this Tribunal cannot adjudicate the 
dispute in the absence of reference of termination by retrenchment of Petitioner. Thus, Reference is answered 
accordingly. 


Award is passed accordingly. Transmit.
